Let’s look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics. First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example, They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.
